question: When other players share the world, does the creator play an open role everyone can see, or a hidden role (imposter, secret saboteur) whose fun is the deception itself?
pole_low: open role: everyone in the world knows what he is
pole_high: hidden role: secret mission, cover story, fun is not getting caught
why: UnspeakablePlays' third sampled video is built entirely on a hidden role: covert saboteurs inside their own server, hiding tools, lying in chat, absorbing capture without breaking cover. None of the existing role questions separate hidden from open roles, yet for a multiplayer avatar the difference decides whether scenes are played as performance or as espionage.
evidence_needed: Multiplayer videos per creator; look for sustained cover behaviour, knowledge hidden from other players, and capture/absorption beats.

question: Are audience asks (subscribe, like) ever turned into bets on the video's own outcome, so the ask becomes a stake in the game rather than an appeal beside it?
pole_low: asks are appeals: watchers are asked to support the channel
pole_high: asks are wagers: each button backs an outcome and the video settles the bet
why: MoreAliA's third sampled video ties subscribe to one race outcome and like to the other, then resolves the bet on camera at the close. That is a step beyond asks-as-content (renergy-004): the audience is given a side. For Our Guy it turns the frame itself into a game the viewer is playing.
evidence_needed: Reaction and challenge formats; look for asks tied to a stated outcome and settled on camera before the video ends.
